language.script: Hangul exclusively — Hanja (Chinese characters) has been officially phased out of everyday use since the 1950s, unlike South Korea

terrainDescription.zh: 地形以山地為主（尤其北部與東部），西部沿海有較集中的平原農業區
terrainDescription.en: Predominantly mountainous, especially in the north and east, with denser coastal agricultural plains in the west

plate.color: blue background/white text for most state-owned vehicles (most common on the road); yellow background/black text for private and foreign-resident vehicles; black, longer-format plates for military use

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Not documented — on-the-ground photographic and Street View access is essentially nonexistent, so this isn't a usable clue in practice

utilityPole.transformerMount: Not independently confirmed — inferred as broadly similar to other regional Soviet/Chinese-influenced infrastructure; treat as low-confidence

historicalContext.zh: 北韓自1950年代起全面廢止漢字於日常書寫的使用，僅保留諺文（韓文字母），與南韓形成鮮明對比；由於實體踏勘與街景資料極度稀少，本頁資料信心度整體偏低。
historicalContext.en: North Korea has fully phased Hanja (Chinese characters) out of everyday writing since the 1950s, using Hangul exclusively — a sharp contrast with South Korea. On-the-ground photographic/Street View data is extremely scarce, so confidence for this entry is lower overall.
